patterns_found.visual_evidence: The desktop sketch shows a distinct top header/title area with a horizontal navigation row directly beneath it, separated from the body by a long horizontal rule. This layout strongly suggests a persistent top navigation bar that remains available while reading long-form content.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Navigation should remain fixed or become fixed after scroll so section/context links stay accessible while the user reads the page content.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly show a scrolled state, so it is unclear whether the nav is always fixed or only becomes sticky after passing the header.

sketch_notes: Both sketches primarily depict static article-style content with headings, text blocks, and simple link-like elements. The mobile sketch does not clearly indicate any explicit interactive control such as a hamburger, modal trigger, accordion, or form. The desktop sketch adds a clearer horizontal navigation structure at the top, which implies sticky navigation as the main JavaScript-enhanced behavior. Overall JS complexity appears low, with desktop requiring slightly more interaction support than mobile.
